variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A multimodal AI system combines evidence from different data types, such as text, images, audio, video, or sensor readings, to perform one bounded task. The important word is combines. Accepting several upload fields is not enough; the system must define how the inputs are represented, aligned, fused, trusted, and handled when one source is missing or contradictory.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Complementary evidence
pairs.detail: The sources describe different aspects of one event.
pairs.explanation: The sources describe different aspects of one event. Text supplies intent while an image supplies spatial evidence.

pairs.label: Redundant evidence
pairs.detail: Two sources observe the same property.
pairs.explanation: Two sources observe the same property. Agreement can raise confidence; disagreement must become a visible state.

pairs.label: Correlated noise
pairs.detail: Two modalities may repeat the same bias, timestamp error, or upstream label.
pairs.explanation: Two modalities may repeat the same bias, timestamp error, or upstream label. More inputs do not create independent evidence.

variants.hint:
Complementary evidence: The sources describe different aspects of one event.

Redundant evidence: Two sources observe the same property.

Correlated noise: Two modalities may repeat the same bias, timestamp error, or upstream label.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

variants.prompt: What distinguishes a multimodal system from an API that merely accepts several file types?
options: It defines how evidence is aligned, fused, and handled when a modality is missing or contradictory
It always converts every input into plain text before inference
It requires every modality to have the same number of tokens
It guarantees that adding a modality improves accuracy
variants.explanation: The system contract includes alignment, fusion, contribution, trust, and degraded-input behavior; multiple upload fields alone do not provide those guarantees.

Increase the model temperature

variants.prompt: An image contains text telling the model to override tool policy. How should the application treat it?
options: As untrusted content evidence that cannot grant new instruction or tool authority
As a higher-priority system instruction because it is inside an image
As safe once the image decoder succeeds
As a reason to skip audit logging
variants.explanation: Content extracted from media remains untrusted input. Tool and policy authority must come from the application boundary, not from a modality.
